claims.statement: ADR-0003's owner-operated distribution direction now has a bounded server-side marketplace/catalog slice, while operator-custom trust, a public Provider SDK, external-provider onboarding, and executable modules remain unimplemented and separately gated.

A Game Cartridge is an immutable publisher-signed package of manifest data, declarative screens, pinned view schemas, localization, and bounded assets that only trusted OmarchyGS renderer code can interpret.
Cartridges cannot contain or invoke publisher QML, JavaScript, native code, shell commands, arbitrary shaders, imports, dynamic remote assets, filesystem paths, or network clients.

The isolated Ticket 014 proof verifies Ed25519-signed package contents and bounded declarative nodes, then runs a loopback broker and separate provider process without changing production routes, migrations, registry injection, or the production QML entrypoint.

The proof's provider owns one gameplay revision and returns signed idempotent results, while the broker binds calls to registered identities and short-lived one-scope pairwise grants and returns a sanitized presentation response.

The provider bridge keeps device credentials and raw account or persona IDs inside OmarchyGS, binds each operation to a pairwise subject, one short-lived scope, idempotency key, and expected provider revision, and authenticates exact request, response, and callback bytes.

Production Cartridge Core supports Terminal, Grid, Status, Button, Image, and Meter, while Rich-2D adds Sprite, ParticleField, and AudioCue; advanced 2D/2.5D, constrained 3D, and isolated Web profiles remain separate future reviews.

The intended graphics envelope extends from terminal games through polished animated card, board, tactical, tile, sprite, RPG, strategy, puzzle, and visual-novel experiences, but excludes Halo-class first-person rendering, high-frequency physics, twitch networking, arbitrary publisher rendering code, and a general Unity or Unreal runtime.

Ticket 016 ratifies Core and Rich-2D software-rendering profiles through signed stress fixtures, 60 warm-up frames, 120 measured frames, a 33.3 ms average ceiling, profile RSS caps, and explicit rendered-raster admission ceilings.

The implemented cartridge path now includes the contract, renderer, SDK/release workflow, secure staging, provider pilot, signed marketplace synchronization, atomic reviewed inventory, audited server admission, and an authenticated metadata catalog; client acquisition and launch remain later work.

The production cartridge library and CLI deterministically pack canonical stored-only ZIP archives, verify a domain-separated Ed25519 integrity index over every payload byte, reconstruct the canonical archive, and return immutable authenticated content plus explicit compatibility and provenance without contacting a provider.

Game Cartridge v1 bounds archives, entries, expanded bytes, schemas, presentation nodes, strict 8-bit PNG, and PCM WAV; every screen pins a declared schema and every typed node binds to an exact host capability and node-specific action or asset contract.

The Ticket 015 store installs exact verified archives as read-only content-addressed blobs with atomic activation and revocation records, re-verifies active blobs, fails closed on malformed revocation paths, and is supported only as a same-user local boundary.

The production renderer accepts only an immutable VerifiedCartridge, validates a bounded view against the screen's authenticated restricted schema, applies signed capability fallbacks and trusted preferences, and emits an inert omarchygs.render-plan/v1 document.
Core and Rich-2D enforce incremental plan, node, effect, per-raster, and scene-decoded-raster budgets before publishing any admitted node or asset.

The trusted QML surface accepts only exact plan keys and fixed node kinds, independently recounts aggregate profile budgets, maps kinds to repository-owned Components, and renders cartridge strings as explicit plain text.

The preview CLI verifies the real signed archive, reads bounded regular view and preference files, compiles the production plan, and writes read-only plan and digest-named assets only into an existing empty private directory.

On the final one-CPU software-rendering gate, Core averaged 15.998 ms at 132,688 KiB peak RSS, Rich-2D averaged 16.000 ms at 244,664 KiB, the maximum accepted 2,048-pixel Rich-2D raster averaged 16.006 ms at 250,312 KiB, and the accessibility scene averaged 16.001 ms at 237,864 KiB.
The v1 SDK export is deterministic, read-only, language-neutral, self-verifying, and pins exact schema, tool, protocol, compatibility, deprecation, and retirement identities.
A signed release attestation binds the source revision, builder identity and binary digest, SDK identity, publisher and game identities, exact archive digest, and conformance digest.

The catalog lifecycle has active, deprecated, suspended, revoked, and retired states with explicit new-launch and active-session decisions; signed policy identity and monotonic versions prevent silent release substitution.

The Linux secure importer retains no-follow directory descriptors, validates effective-UID ownership and writable modes, serializes policy transitions under an exclusive descriptor-relative lock, and persists authenticated denial policy before enforcing it.

The provider control plane stores operator-pinned immutable releases and the singleton pilot, lifecycle scopes, append-only signing and TLS keys, short-lived grants, quotas, concurrency leases, durable operation and callback receipts, and safe audit events in PostgreSQL.

Production provider and marketplace egress admit only fixed HTTPS DNS origins whose complete answer sets pass the shared public-unicast classifier, pin accepted sockets with hostname verification, trust explicit roots, and deny proxies, redirects, decompression, reserved ranges, and unbounded responses.
Migration 0015 prevents dual gameplay authority by requiring local object state only for platform_compiled sessions and a null local state plus exact release pin for registered_provider sessions.

The Door Legends bridge persists the platform session envelope and idempotent start receipt before provider I/O, then routes launch, command, and explicit reconcile through the signed broker without holding a session transaction across the network.
Authenticated provider callbacks are deduplicated and policy-checked inside the same PostgreSQL transaction that records allowlisted result, achievement, view, audit, and persona-sync projections.

Suspension denies new launches, commands, and callbacks while retaining read-only session views and explicit reconciliation; restoration requires authenticated reconciliation, and retirement is terminal.

Signal Siege's main-client surface is platform-owned trusted application code that may reuse inert repository node components but does not mint signed cartridge origin, content digest, or omarchygs.render-plan/v1 provenance.

The trusted cartridge preview, surface, and visual node implementations consume the host OgsTheme palette and preserve platform-owned high-contrast, focus, accessibility, reduced-motion, and mute behavior without granting the cartridge executable styling authority.

The server-curated lifecycle now implements marketplace publication intake, immutable reviewed staging, administrator admission, and server-scoped metadata visibility; exact client acquisition, local caching, mounting, and session pinning remain future slices.

An operator-custom cartridge remains signed inert frontend data subject to the same official-client bounds and trusted rendering, while custom backend or general module code executes only server-side through separately designed extension boundaries.

A marketplace snapshot is canonical, bounded, domain-separated, strictly Ed25519-verified by one configured authority, monotonically versioned, and sorted uniquely across exact release digests and relative acquisition paths.

The marketplace client locks scheme, host, port, and relative paths; validates every DNS answer as public unicast; pins sockets; trusts one bounded DER root; and disables proxy, redirect, referer, decompression, pooling, and unbounded bodies.

Synchronization reuses the production release verifier and descriptor-relative secure store, permits immutable unreferenced staging, and advances current reviewed inventory only after the complete snapshot is published in one serialized PostgreSQL transaction.

Marketplace lifecycle and server admission are independent: an expected-state idempotent command selects one exact current permitted digest per game and appends its immutable audit receipt in the same transaction.

The player catalog is authenticated and metadata-only, listing only imported compatible selected releases present in the current snapshot with active or deprecated lifecycle state and no fallback to another digest.
